problem_statement: The CPU frequency on-demand policy fails to switch states when the current CPU load is below the load threshold of every defined P-state. In that situation it returns -ENOTSUP and the CPU gets stuck in its current (often high-performance) P-state instead of scaling down to the lowest performance state. The policy should instead select the last P-state in the configured list (the one with the lowest load threshold, i.e. the lowest performance state) whenever no threshold is matched, so that the CPU can always scale down at low load. The P-states must be defined in devicetree in decreasing load_threshold order so that this last P-state is the lowest performance one.
